comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RCA (Phase 1 complete — proven root cause, runtime-confirmed)

STALE CITATION IN THIS TICKET: the description points at
`adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`. Ticket 465d's one-module-per-capability split has since
landed; `_paged_search` now lives at
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:120-157`
(class `_TransportBase`, the shared pager every capability mixin inherits). The defect moved
with it verbatim.

ROOT CAUSE (two coupled mechanisms, one artifact each):

M1 — the pager loop has no offset-stall guard. `_base.py:141-157`:

    out = []; start_at = 0
    while True:
        results = _call_logged("_paged_search", jql, lambda offset=start_at: ...)
        batch = [_unwrap(i) for i in results]
        if not batch: break          # <-- the ONLY exit
        out.extend(batch)
        start_at += len(batch)

`start_at` advances locally, but nothing checks that the SERVER honoured it. A DC instance
that ignores/repeats `startAt` re-serves the same non-empty page forever, so `batch` is never
empty and the only exit is unreachable: an unbounded loop with `out` growing without limit.

M2 — the fail-open handler would swallow a loud abort. `_hierarchy.py:91`
(`get_parent_map`) wraps the `_paged_search` drain in a bare
`except Exception: log warning; return {}` degradation contract. Any error the pager raises is
converted into a silent EMPTY parent map — i.e. the loud signal M1's fix adds would be
neutralised at this caller unless it is re-raised ahead of the broad clause, exactly as the
Cloud sibling does (`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:304-306, 394-396, 477`).

DISCRIMINATING RUNTIME EVIDENCE (not static reading — the hypothesis is dynamic):

Experiment 1 (M1) — drove the real `_paged_search` with a `startAt`-ignoring stub that serves
the same 3-issue page for every request, plus a 25-call harness cap to bound the run:
  RESULT: 26 calls. Offsets REQUESTED = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, ...] — the client
  kept advancing while the server kept serving page 1. Terminated only by the harness cap, not
  by the pager. Predicted-if-true outcome exactly; a guarded pager would have stopped at 2.

Experiment 2 (M2) — same stub through `get_parent_map`:
  RESULT: returned `{}` after 26 calls, raising nothing. Confirms the fail-open path is live
  and converts a pager-level abort into a silent empty map (the differ then treats every issue
  as parentless).

Alternatives ruled out: not `_call_logged`/retry (it re-raises untouched, `_base.py:60-66`);
not the short-page/truncation defect (bug 9263 — that one is already fixed here and the
offsets prove the loop IS advancing its request, so the failure is server-side offset
blindness, a different axis); not a caller-side loop (all three callers drain the shared pager,
`_links.py:39`, `_links.py:87`, `_hierarchy.py:78` — there is exactly one loop).

LEGITIMACY = defect, against three cited authorities in this same codebase:
1. `fetcher.py:336-344` — the SAME operation (offset-paged whole-project issue search) on a
   parallel surface RAISES `SilentTruncationError(reason="offset-stall")` on exactly this
   condition, and states the rule as a documented contract at `fetcher.py:275-277`. Design
   invariant.
2. `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:29-46, 79-86` — the Cloud sibling raises
   `RunawayPaginationError` on a stalled cursor and its readers re-raise past their fail-open
   handlers. Prior CLOSED `Fixed:` bug cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c for this same class (commit
   30c522cde9).
3. `_base.py:131-139` — this pager's own docstring claims a structural test prevents a further
   unguarded instance of the class; that guard covers only the page-size axis, not offset stall.

PARITY CENSUS (Step-7 Axis 2) — rule: "an offset/cursor-paged whole-project search must abort
loudly when the server stops advancing":
- `fetcher._iter_pages` (offset)          -> HOLDS, `fetcher.py:336-344`
- `acli_graph._iter_cursor_pages` (cursor) -> HOLDS, `acli_graph.py:79-86`
- `jira_datacenter/_base._paged_search`    -> **MISSING** (this ticket)
- `_issues.py:257-263` / `acli.py:448`     -> N/A: single-page primitives, not pagers; the
  loop that drives them is `fetcher._iter_pages`, already guarded.
Exactly one MISSING slot. No further siblings.

CALLER-DEPENDENCY GATE: callers are `get_issuelinks_map` (`_links.py:39`), `get_comment_map`
(`_links.py:87`), `get_parent_map` (`_hierarchy.py:78`). None depends on the spin. The one
deliberate behaviour change is M2 — `get_parent_map` stops fail-opening on a stall — which is
acceptance criterion 2 and matches the Cloud precedent. Gate passes.

FIX PLAN (narrow by design; ticket 465d owns re-architecting these modules and another stream
owns `set_parent`/parent handling, so the diff stays minimal):
1. `_base.py` — add a dedicated `RunawayPaginationError(RuntimeError)` beside the pager, and
   track the previous page's first issue key in `_paged_search`. If a page repeats the previous
   page's first key, raise it: the server is not honouring `startAt`, so paging can never
   advance. Raises on the SECOND call.
   DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from `fetcher.py:335-345`: fetcher returns cleanly (no raise) when the
   repeated page is SHORT, reasoning that a client returning fewer items than asked and then
   repeating itself "has nothing further to give". That reasoning does NOT transfer to DC. This
   pager exists (bug 9263) precisely because a hardened DC caps EVERY page below the requested
   size via `jira.search.views.default.max` — so on DC a short page is the NORMAL case with more
   to give, and adopting fetcher's short-page branch would silently return 20 of 250 (the exact
   92%-loss defect this pager was built to refuse). `_paged_search` therefore raises on ANY
   repeated page, short or full. It cannot false-positive: a `startAt`-honouring server serves
   DIFFERENT issues at each offset.
2. `_hierarchy.py` — add `except RunawayPaginationError: raise` immediately ahead of
   `get_parent_map`'s broad `except Exception`, mirroring `acli_graph.py:304-306`.
3. `transport.py` — re-export the error through the existing `__all__` facade (2 lines only;
   no other change to that file).
4. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — the RED oracle: a
   `startAt`-ignoring stub proving loud self-termination within 2 calls, that the error escapes
   `get_parent_map`'s fail-open, and that well-behaved page-capping servers still recover 250/250.

comments.body:
PHASE 2 COMPLETE — fix pushed for review as Gerrit change 1395 (NOT closed; epic coordinator verifies).
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1395  (commit f078af4a65)

TEST (RED -> GREEN, held out, with teeth)
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py — +244 lines, purely
additive (0 lines removed; no pre-existing test touched or weakened).

RED first, for the RIGHT reason: 6 failed / 15 passed. The two pager cases failed with
"the pager made 26 calls against a startAt-ignoring server — it never self-terminated
(offsets requested: [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27]...)", and all four fail-open cases
with "DID NOT RAISE" — the captured log showing our own error being absorbed into
"snapshot written without issuelink data (degraded)". An initial run failed on a collection
ImportError, which is NOT a legitimate RED; the exception type (the oracle's contract
surface) was declared first so the RED came from behaviour.

The oracle was then MOVED OUT of the tree (git stash) before the fix subagent was launched;
the subagent got only the frozen contract card, never the test. On restore it was verified
byte-identical (diff clean — the fixer never touched it). GREEN: 21 passed, exit 0.

MUTATION CHECKS (3, all returned the oracle to RED, fix restored after each)
1. M1 re-introduced verbatim (pristine pre-fix loop restored): 3 failed / 18 passed —
   exactly the pager + get_parent_map cases, at 26 calls. Negative controls stayed GREEN,
   so the mutation is faithful. (A first, cruder excision left a dangling reference and went
   red via NameError; that was discarded and redone as a verbatim revert.)
2. M2 re-introduced (all four `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` clauses deleted):
   4 failed / 17 passed — each of the four fail-open sites caught individually.
3. NEAR-MISS, the trap: adopt fetcher's short-page branch (`if len(batch) < page_size:
   return out`) — the superficially plausible fix. 2 failed / 19 passed: the oracle REJECTS
   it on the SHORT-page case. This is the strongest teeth evidence, since that branch is
   exactly what copying `fetcher.py:335-345` would have produced.

Refactoring litmus: every assertion is on observable behaviour (raised type, client call
count at the injected boundary, snapshot file contents, `__all__` membership — the latter
being documented contract). No source-text greps, no private names. Renaming an internal
in `_paged_search` breaks nothing.

FIX (6 files; scope kept narrow for the parallel streams on 465d and set_parent)
- `_backend.py` (+24) — `BackendPaginationStallError(RuntimeError)`. In CORE because
  `fetcher` must name it and core must never import `adapters/`; an adapter-local error
  would be unnameable at exactly the boundary that absorbs it.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py` (+39) — the guard in `_paged_search`: track the
  previous page's first key, raise on ANY repeat. Message names `startAt`, the stalled
  offset, the repeated key and the JQL. Guarded against keyless/non-dict heads so two
  consecutive keyless pages cannot fire a spurious `None == None` stall.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py` (+10/-1) — the re-raise ahead of
  `get_parent_map`'s broad clause. `set_parent` untouched.
- `fetcher.py` (+25) — the re-raise ahead of all three `fetch_snapshot` enrichment
  handlers. Import is module-level ABSOLUTE (a relative one breaks: this module is loaded
  standalone via importlib in tests).
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (+9/-1) — facade re-export only, 2 effective
  lines. No other change to the file 465d owns.
- the test file above.
All files under the locked 800-line cap (fetcher.py is the closest at 771, was 746).

GATES (real exit codes, captured directly — not piped through tail)
- `make lint` -> 0   (first run was 2: ruff format on my new test block; fixed)
- `make typecheck` -> 0
- held-out oracle -> 0 (21 passed)
- `pytest tests/unit` -> 8107 passed, 28 skipped, 1 error. The single error is a HARNESS
  ARTIFACT OF THIS SESSION, not a regression: `test_lock_stale_reclaim.py::
  test_acquire_does_not_reclaim_live_owner` guards against the repo HEAD moving mid-run,
  and I committed the fix while the 22-minute suite was still running
  ("Test moved the repo HEAD (fc705c6441 -> f078af4a65)"). Re-run with a stable HEAD:
  24 passed, exit 0.
- `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` -> OK, resolved 18a4-9df8-6373-4d9f.

REPLICATION of the original report (the deciding evidence)
- Report scenario (offset-blind DC): 26 calls, offsets [0,3,6,...] -> now 2 calls
  [0, 3] and a named `BackendPaginationStallError`.
- Fail-open swallow: `get_parent_map` returning a silent `{}` after 26 calls -> now the
  error propagates (traceback through `_hierarchy.py:83` -> `_base.py:187`).
The original report no longer reproduces.

SIBLING SWEEP (both axes)
Axis 1 (construct) — exhaustive, not bounded: the whole reconciler contains exactly THREE
unbounded loops (`grep -rn "while True:"`), and all three are the pagers already accounted
for: `fetcher.py:294` (guarded, bug deac), `_base.py:168` (this fix),
`acli_graph.py:67` (guarded, bug cabc). There is no fourth instance.
Axis 2 (parity) — one MISSING slot, fixed here. `_issues.py:262` / `acli.py:448` are N/A
(single-page primitives, not pagers; the loop driving them is the guarded
`fetcher._iter_pages`).

RESIDUAL RISK — dispositioned
1. TICKET FILED 9a46-1c90-5dd9-44e1 (linked discovered_from): Cloud's
   `acli_graph.RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by these SAME three fetcher handlers —
   `grep -n "RunawayPagination" fetcher.py` returns NOTHING, so bug cabc's fix is itself
   incomplete at the fetcher boundary. Proposed one-line fix recorded: subclass the new
   core error. Not folded in — it changes CLOUD-surface behaviour, owned elsewhere.
2. TICKET FILED 34c2-8c41-1a12-4254 (linked discovered_from): the structural guard
   `test_no_search_issues_call_relies_on_the_default_page_size` has gone VACUOUS. It
   AST-scans `transport.py` only, and 465d's split moved every `search_issues` call out —
   MEASURED: 0 such calls remain in that file, so the guard passes unconditionally and
   would not catch a fifth unpaginated caller. Notable because its sibling's own docstring
   says "a structural test that cannot fail is decoration". Not fixed here: it is 465d
   fallout and widening a guard's scope can surface unrelated offenders.
3. ACCEPTED: `fetcher.py` is now 771/800 lines. Under the cap but the tightest headroom of
   any file touched; the next addition there should split rather than append.

STALE CITATION corrected in the description: the ticket pointed at
`adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`; the pager now lives at
`adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py`.

compiled_state.description:
Sibling of cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c, found in its Phase-1 sibling sweep (E5). Jira DC's shared pager
`_paged_search` loops on `startAt` offsets with no stall guard. A server that ignores/repeats
`startAt` (returns the same page) spins forever — measured: 26 calls to the experiment harness cap
— instead of terminating loudly. Same defect class as cabc (Cloud acli_graph cursor spin, fixed by
ab7f in 30c522cde9) and `fetcher._iter_pages` (guarded since bug deac).

CORRECTED LOCATION: the original description cited `adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`. Ticket
465d's one-module-per-capability split has since landed and moved the pager verbatim to
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:120-157` (`_TransportBase`,
the shared pager every capability mixin inherits).

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; full RCA in the ticket comments)

M1 — `_base.py:141-157`: the pager's ONLY loop exit is `if not batch: break`. `start_at` advances
locally but nothing verifies the SERVER honoured it, so an offset-blind instance re-serves the same
non-empty page forever and the exit is unreachable (`out` grows unbounded). Runtime evidence: a
`startAt`-ignoring stub drove 26 calls, requesting offsets [0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27,...] while
receiving page 1 every time; terminated only by the harness cap.

M2 — `_hierarchy.py:91`: `get_parent_map` wraps the drain in a bare
`except Exception: warn; return {}` degradation contract, which converts any pager-level abort into
a SILENT empty parent map. Runtime evidence: the same stub returned `{}` after 26 calls, raising
nothing. So M1's loud signal is neutralised at this caller unless re-raised ahead of the broad clause.

Legitimacy = defect, against cited authority: `fetcher.py:336-344` (the same operation on a
parallel surface raises `SilentTruncationError(reason="offset-stall")`, contract stated at
`fetcher.py:275-277`), `acli_graph.py:29-46, 79-86` (the Cloud sibling raises
`RunawayPaginationError` and its readers re-raise past fail-open at `acli_graph.py:304-306`), and
the prior CLOSED `Fixed:` bug cabc for this same class.

## Plan

Scope is deliberately narrow — ticket 465d owns re-architecting the DC transport modules and
another stream owns `set_parent`/parent handling — but the EDIT SET IS NOT ONE RE-RAISE. Plan
review (T4/T5b/G1G2) correctly found that `_paged_search` feeds THREE whole-project readers and
that ALL THREE are consumed by `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` behind broad `except Exception` fail-open
handlers (`fetcher.py:610` parent, `fetcher.py:652` comment, `fetcher.py:688` issuelink). VERIFIED:
`fetcher.py` names neither stall error (grep for `RunawayPagination` there returns nothing), so a
stall raised in the transport is swallowed at the fetcher boundary and the pass writes a silently
degraded snapshot. A guard that stops at the transport boundary would therefore NOT resolve the
original report. There are FOUR fail-open sites to pierce, not one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ERROR TYPE (also plan-review advisory A1: do not mint a third bespoke error for
one class). `fetcher.py` is CORE and must be able to name the error, but core must never import
adapters — verified: `fetcher.py` imports nothing from `adapters/`, while adapters already import
`BackendEnvError`/`BackendHTTPError` FROM core (`_links.py:19`, `transport.py:66`). So the error
belongs in core's `_backend.py` beside the other `Backend*` errors, where both the DC adapter and
`fetcher` can name it with no layering inversion — one canonical type for the class rather than a
third bespoke one.

1. `_backend.py` — add `BackendPaginationStallError(RuntimeError)` beside the existing `Backend*`
   errors (`_backend.py:38-60`). Docstring states the invariant: a paged whole-project read whose
   server stopped advancing is a TRUNCATED read, and readers must re-raise it past their fail-open
   handlers rather than degrade around it.
2. `_base.py` — in `_paged_search`, remember the previous page's first issue key; if a page repeats
   it, raise `BackendPaginationStallError`. The server is not honouring `startAt`, so paging can
   never advance. Fires on the SECOND call.
   DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from `fetcher.py:335-345`: fetcher returns cleanly (no raise) when the
   repeated page is SHORT, reasoning a client that returns fewer items than asked and then repeats
   "has nothing further to give". That does NOT transfer to DC. This pager exists (bug 9263)
   precisely because a hardened DC caps EVERY page below the requested size via
   `jira.search.views.default.max` — so on DC a short page is the NORMAL case WITH more to give, and
   adopting fetcher's short-page branch would silently return 20 of 250: the exact 92%-loss defect
   this pager was built to refuse. `_paged_search` therefore raises on ANY repeated page, short or
   full. It cannot false-positive: a `startAt`-honouring server serves DIFFERENT issues per offset.
3. `_hierarchy.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` immediately ahead of
   `get_parent_map`'s broad `except Exception` (`_hierarchy.py:91`), mirroring `acli_graph.py:304-306`.
4. `fetcher.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` ahead of each of the three broad
   `except Exception` enrichment handlers (`fetcher.py:610`, `:652`, `:688`). This is the boundary
   that decides whether the whole pass fails loudly or writes a degraded snapshot, and a stall must
   fail loudly: consumer confirmed — `fetch_snapshot`'s caller is the reconciler pass, which has no
   `{}`-specific expectation for these enrichments (each is guarded by `hasattr` and merges only
   what it gets), so the propagated error aborts the pass with the transport's own
   `_call_logged` WARNING already emitted (`_base.py:60-66`) plus the raised message — instrumented,
   not an uninstrumented traceback.
5. `transport.py` — re-export `BackendPaginationStallError` through the existing `__all__` facade
   (2 lines; no other change to that file, which 465d owns).
6. Tests — the RED oracle (see Verification).

NOT IN SCOPE, ticket to be filed and linked `discovered_from`: Cloud's own
`acli_graph.RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by these SAME three fetcher handlers, so bug cabc's
fix (commit 30c522cde9) is itself incomplete at the fetcher boundary. Making Cloud stalls propagate
is a behaviour change on the Cloud surface owned by another stream, so it is filed rather than
folded in here.

## Verification

RED→GREEN with the oracle held out from the implementing subagent, plus a defect-seeded mutation
check (re-remove the guard -> the test must return RED). Oracle lives in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` and covers: a
`startAt`-ignoring stub proving loud self-termination within 2 calls; the error escaping
`get_parent_map`'s fail-open; the error escaping all three `fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers;
the facade import; and the unchanged 250/250 recovery for well-behaved page-capping servers through
all three whole-project readers. Then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the DC + fetcher +
acli_graph pagination suites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_paged_search` raises a dedicated runaway/stall error when `startAt` does not advance
- [ ] Fail-open exception handling does not swallow the stall error at ANY of the four sites: the
      transport's own `get_parent_map`, and all three `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers
- [ ] Held-out test with a `startAt`-ignoring stub proves termination within 2 calls
- [ ] The stall error is re-exported and importable through the `transport.py` facade
- [ ] Existing DC pagination behaviour for well-behaved servers unchanged (250/250 still recovered
      from a page-capping client through all three whole-project readers), and the pre-existing
      `get_parent_map` fail-open contract still returns `{}` for ORDINARY failures

the offset-stall guard inside _paged_search (the defect site)
re-raise the stall error ahead of get_parent_map fail-open handler
re-raise the stall error ahead of the three fetch_snapshot enrichment fail-open handlers (610/652/688)
re-export the error through the existing __all__ facade (2 lines)
RED oracle: startAt-ignoring stub proves loud termination within 2 calls and escape past all four fail-open sites

compiled_state.title: DC _paged_search lacks offset-stall guard (runaway pagination sibling)
